style: Style: an original illustration in the manner of an 18th-century Southeast Asian palm-leaf and folding-book manuscript painting (parabaik / samut khoi) and 18th-century temple mural line art: fine black ink contour lines, flat areas of a few natural pigments only (red ochre, indigo, muted green, touches of gold leaf, chalk white), on warm aged khoi-paper texture with soft stains. Head-and-shoulders bust, three-quarter view, centred, facing slightly left, dignified and respectful. Plain aged-paper background fading to the edges, no scenery. Historically plausible late-18th-century Burmese (Konbaung dynasty) dress and hairstyle: hair worn long in a topknot, gaung baung head-wrap or court headdress, Burmese court jackets. Not photorealistic, not anime, not a game character. No text, no letters, no seals, no signature, no border.

items.azaewungyi: Maha Thiha Thura (known in Thai as Azaewungyi), a senior Burmese general of the Konbaung court in his fifties: weathered, shrewd, commanding face, deep-set calm eyes, greying moustache; wearing a white gaung baung head-wrap and a dark long-sleeved Burmese military court jacket with gold edging; a veteran who has defeated the Qing army.
items.hsinbyushin: King Hsinbyushin of Burma (Konbaung dynasty), in his late thirties: proud, stern royal face, thin moustache; wearing a tall tiered golden Burmese royal crown and a richly gold-embroidered royal jacket with flared shoulder pieces; depicted with dignity, as in a royal mural.
